description: Phase 3 resize/maximize/restore smoke budget for the boot-smoke-tests DWM kernel (limine_test_gui.conf embeds assets/dwm/test.toml). test.toml's [startup] autostarts two gui_clients (proving the M3 cross-process isolation invariant — two untrusted clients composited at once) plus gui_terminal + gui_files, and sets `self_test = true`. With self_test on, the compositor drives EVERY live window through the SAME `set_window_state` path the title-bar maximize chip and the macOS-style drag-to-restore use — a server-push CONFIGURE — first MAXIMIZING each window (work-area-sized re-import across a real process boundary), then after a short settle RESTORING it to its floating geometry (the reverse CONFIGURE). Maximizing all windows (not just runtime-pumped ones) keeps the proof independent of which clients present first. `served two untrusted clients OK` + `desktop ready` prove the desktop came up; `acked (self-test)` proves the compositor pushed the maximize; `restored (self-test)` proves the un-maximize round trip works; `gui_terminal/gui_files: reconfigured OK` prove BOTH heavier clients re-negotiated their buffer at the new geometry. Run: tools/qemu_test.py --build --config limine_test_gui.conf --markers-file tools/gui_smoke_markers.json --ready-marker 'gui_server: desktop ready' --timeout 300 --linger 8. The GUI kernel never prints [TERM-007], so --ready-marker MUST be overridden as shown. `--linger` keeps collecting serial past `desktop ready` so the restore leg (which happens a few ticks after the maximize completes, i.e. after the ready milestone) is captured.

required.marker: gui_server: served two untrusted clients OK
required.claim: two untrusted gui_clients composited at once (M3 isolation invariant preserved)
compositor reached an interactive, presenting state
M4 schema versioning: test.toml declares [meta] schema_version=1 and this build supports it
M4 forward-compat guard: version_supported() accepts current, rejects future+0 (newer doc → last-known-good baseline, never mis-parsed)

M4 window/session restore: the compositor remembered every live window's geometry, wrote the session store, reloaded it, and every id/x/y/w/h matched — the save→persist→reload path works across a real file

M4 Alt/Super-Tab window switcher: with [shortcuts] switcher on, the compositor armed the SAME Switcher state the key-drain path uses, advanced off the front window, committed, and raising the highlight made a DIFFERENT window the topmost/focused one — the switch is real, not cosmetic

required.marker: gui_server: notify posted added=1 corner=1 timeout_ms=3000 ok
required.claim: M4 desktop notifications: with [notifications] enabled, the compositor posted a toast through the SAME notify_post queue the app-launch sites use; policy (corner=1, timeout_ms=3000) came entirely from config, this post enqueued exactly one toast (delta-checked, independent of any client's live startup toast), and the queued toast survived the prune while a synthetic future-tick expired it — the transient is real, not cosmetic

M4 notification auto-dismiss end-to-end: after timeout_ms/16 frames the per-frame retain() pruned the posted toast and the queue drained to empty on its own — the config-driven timeout actually fires, not just parses

M4 quick-settings applet: with [quicksettings] enabled, the panel applet flipped the LIVE fx.blur/wg.enabled fields the renderer reads (single source of truth, no shadow copy) and restored them — the toggles drive real compositor state

keyboard control: with [shortcuts] cmd_mod policy, match_shortcut() maps cmd_mod+digit→workspace, +Space→launcher, +Q→close, +M→maximize (and bare keys do NOT fire globally), and a behavioural workspace jump applied+read back — the shortcut decision is real, config-driven, and drives live compositor state
compositor pushed a server-initiated CONFIGURE to a runtime window via set_window_state (maximize)
compositor pushed the reverse CONFIGURE to un-maximize the window back to its floating geometry (the user-visible restore, same path the chip and drag-to-restore drive)
the terminal re-imported a work-area-sized buffer in response to CONFIGURE (protocol resize across a process boundary)
the file manager re-imported a work-area-sized buffer in response to CONFIGURE (protocol resize across a process boundary)
the terminal resolved [terminal] bg_alpha=210 from apps/gui_terminal.toml and chose the ARGB8888 presentation format (translucent background, config-driven)

the terminal resolved [terminal] theme=catppuccin_mocha from apps/gui_terminal.toml against the shared term_theme preset table (single source of truth with the kernel terminal); the palette is theme-driven, not hardcoded

required.marker: gui_files: cfg from_file=1 icon_theme=<desktop> bg=0xFF121820 accent=0xFF2F8F5A bg_alpha=235
required.claim: the file manager resolved [files] from apps/gui_files.toml (color scheme + translucent bg_alpha=235) and drives its palette/format from config, not hardcoded constants
the calculator resolved [calc] from apps/gui_calc.toml (bg came from config, from_file=1) and drives its palette from config, not hardcoded constants
the calculator completed the gui-v1 handshake and the compositor presented its first frame (a real untrusted client surface)
the calculator re-imported a work-area-sized buffer in response to CONFIGURE (protocol resize across a process boundary — the modern resizable calculator honours maximize/restore)
the demo/tests app resolved [demo] from apps/gui_demo.toml (palette + bg_alpha) and drives its colors from config, not hardcoded constants
the demo app completed the gui-v1 handshake and the compositor presented its first frame (the dock's gui_client test window is now a real app)
the demo app posted a NOTIFY control message to the compositor at startup (client→compositor notification request across a process boundary)

Subtask 2 end-to-end: the compositor received the demo's NOTIFY message and turned it into a toast through the SAME notify_post path a launch uses — policy ([notifications] enabled/timeout/corner) stayed compositor-owned, the client only named the text (bounds-clamped, untrusted)

scheduler/resource-leak fix: after closing every window the per-frame reaper pruned the clients Vec (freeing spawn slots + protocol connections + shared-buffer mappings), and relaunching succeeded — closing many windows no longer permanently blocks opening new ones

feature #2 (settings resolution picker): with self_test on, gui_settings actuated the SAME apply(ResNext) path a `>` click drives, walked the picker to a concrete non-boot mode (1600x900), wrote it to [display] and pinged reload — the settings UI edits the live resolution, config-driven, no hardcoded mode

feature #2 end-to-end: the compositor received gui_settings' reload ping, diffed the new [display] against the applied mode, and re-entered run_desktop_session to re-apply it — a GUI resolution edit really drives a live session re-entry (the compositor owns the display; the client only edited config)

feature #2 real behavior change: after the re-entry the compositor asked the kernel display backend to mode-set to the picker-chosen 1600x900 (distinct from the 1280x720 boot mode) — the resolution actually changed live via the Settings UI, not just parsed
the compositor performed a per-pixel src-over composite of a translucent (ARGB8888) client instead of an opaque copy

Subtask 4: a classic terminal-mode program (calc) runs under dsh's cooked line discipline via spawn_external — the exact gui_terminal→dsh→child path — echoing keystrokes and delivering whole lines just like kernel Terminal Mode, so the GUI terminal has backward compatibility with terminal programs
